description: Figure 5 is a bar chart illustrating the performance gain (expressed as a percentage, +%) achieved on various tasks through the use of predictive rollout search within the VisuoThink framework. The performance gain is quantified as the difference in performance between VisuoThink with predictive rollout search and VisuoThink without it. The horizontal axis lists distinct task categories, likely grouped into geometry and spatial reasoning tasks as referenced in the accompanying text, though the specific task labels are not visible in the provided image. The vertical axis represents the percentage gain, ranging from 0% upward, with tick marks indicating incremental values (e.g., 10%, 20%, etc.), though exact scale markings are not legible. Each bar corresponds to a specific task or task group, with bar heights reflecting the magnitude of performance improvement. The chart visually demonstrates that predictive rollouts yield more substantial gains in spatial reasoning tasks compared to geometry tasks, as indicated by taller bars for spatial tasks. The bars are likely color-coded or grouped to distinguish between open-source and closed-source model variants, as mentioned in the text, though specific color assignments or groupings cannot be discerned from the placeholder image. The overall trend supports the paper’s claim that stronger supervision in spatial tasks leads to greater effectiveness of predictive rollouts.
